title: What are Kearney, Roland Berger, L.E.K. and other strategy firms like to interview with?
description: A quick guide to interviewing at Kearney, Roland Berger, L.E.K., OC&C and Simon-Kucher: what makes each process distinctive.
hook: Beyond MBB and the Big Four sits a group of excellent strategy firms, each with its own strengths and quirks. They are often less crowded with applicants, and many people find their culture or specialism a better fit. Here is what makes each process distinctive.
body:
Kearney

Known for operations and implementation alongside strategy. Prep guides describe a separate, graded fit interview where structured stories (situation, task, action, result) matter, and stories that end in real results go down well. Kearney also publishes a practice case on its website.

Roland Berger

A European-rooted strategy firm with offices in more than 30 countries. Cases are usually candidate-led and fit and case interviews are often separate. Some final rounds include a group case.

L.E.K. Consulting

Strong in life sciences and private equity work. The process often includes a written case, so practise reading a data pack quickly and presenting a clear answer. Market sizing comes up often.

OC&C and Simon-Kucher

OC&C is a strategy firm known for consumer and retail work. Simon-Kucher specialises in pricing and growth, so expect pricing to feature heavily. Both publish practice material.

How to approach these firms

  • Learn what each firm is known for, and say why that work appeals to you.
  • Prepare for written and group formats as well as live cases.
  • Network: smaller firms often weigh personal contact and genuine interest heavily.

Sources

  • Road to Offer: firm-specific guides (Kearney, L.E.K.)
  • Hacking the Case Interview: Roland Berger case interview
  • StrategyCase: case interview examples from the firms

Checked November 2026.
